era_note: Davenant wrote in the early seventeenth century as Lady Margaret Professor at Cambridge and Bishop of Salisbury; he was a British delegate at Dort. This is not a patristic work. It is a public-domain Latin Reformed retrieval on the same Fathers-site pipeline. Do not treat the site as ante-Nicene only.
first_english_note: No complete public-domain English of this 1650 Latin Dissertationes duae was locked as reading text. Allport 1831 is an English Colossians commentary, not this work, and was not used. This is a new rendering from locked Latin for the De morte Christi Cap. 1 tip only.

text_history.method: English follows locked 1650 Cambridge Latin of De morte Christi Cap. 1-6 opening (origin + Thesis 1 + Cap. 2 Rat. 1-ultima + Cap. 3 Satisfit through Obj. 17 + Cap. 4 Thesis 2 tip through Mem. 1 close + Cap. 4 Mem. 2 through Mem. 3 tip + Cap. 4 Mem. 3 possible-faith through Thesis 2 close + Cap. 5 Thesis 3 tip through Mem. 2 Scripture close + Cap. 5 Mem. 2 Rat. 1-4 + Cap. 5 Mem. 2 Fathers tip + Cap. 5 Mem. 2 Huberiana objections tip through Obj. 3 Solut close + Cap. 5 Mem. 2 elect-from-eternity objections tip through Obj. 3 Solut close + Cap. 5 Mem. 2 Scripture elect objections tip through Cap. 5 thesis close + Cap. 6 opening tip through Arg. 1 close before Arg. 2), reconstructed from the Internet Archive PDF (pdftotext + tesseract) of the Roger Daniel folio with DjVu OCR check. The 1683 reprint was not used as copy-text. No modern English was copied.
